bug_semantics: Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL took the directory of the file being edited and interpolated it verbatim into the PowerShell program -NoExit -Command "Set-Location -Path '<directory>'". A Windows directory name may contain a single quote, so an attacker-controlled directory can terminate the PowerShell single-quoted literal and append PowerShell statements. When a victim opens a file from that directory and invokes Open PowerShell/Open Terminal (including the administrator variant), ShellExecuteW starts powershell.exe and executes the injected statements with the victim's privileges.
flaw_origin: Commit 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 converted the existing Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL scaffold from a cmd.exe invocation to powershell.exe and first added the vulnerable Set-Location command template using strFolder.c_str() without PowerShell single-quote escaping. Its immediate parent still constructed a cmd.exe '/k cd /d' command and had neither the PowerShell Set-Location template nor the vulnerable single-quoted interpolation.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names Masaru Tsuchiyama <m.tmatma@gmail.com> as both author and committer; its message is only 'powershell の起動に対応' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party lifecycle: https://jvn.jp/en/jp/JVN74538868/ identifies CVE-2026-59561/CWE-78, says the current-directory string is not neutralized, describes the crafted-directory -> victim opens file -> Open Terminal -> arbitrary-command path, and sets the patched product boundary at v2.4.3. The repository advisory https://github.com/sakura-editor/sakura/security/advisories/GHSA-6x2x-729r-wjh5 specifically names Open PowerShell and Open PowerShell as Administrator; https://github.com/sakura-editor/sakura/releases/tag/v2.4.3 lists the corresponding security fix.

Smallest BIC: `git show 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 -- sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` shows the exact causal edit in Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL: `AppendStringF(L"/k cd /d \"%s\"", strFolder.c_str())` became `AppendStringF(L"-NoExit -Command \"Set-Location -Path '%s'\"", strFolder.c_str())`, and ShellExecuteW's executable changed to powershell.exe. This non-merge, single-parent commit wrote the unsafe language boundary itself; the later merge c18e549fcb7c877bf57287cea857a6ef7d49898b merely aggregated the visible feature commits.

History cross-check: `git log -L '/void CViewCommander::Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL/,/^}/':sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` traces the vulnerable template to 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7. Subsequent commits in that line history change comments/types/refactoring but retain the same unescaped strFolder template until the security fix, so neither the later merge nor the 2025 file move is the BIC.

Immediate-parent absence: `git cat-file -p 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7` gives sole parent de6749296b8b9a3ffa2c281d26758770a956f31a. A direct `git diff de6749296b8b9a3ffa2c281d26758770a956f31a 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 -- sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` shows the parent used cmd.exe with `/k cd /d "%s"`; the BIC adds both powershell.exe and `Set-Location -Path '%s'`. Thus the advisory's vulnerable PowerShell interpolation is absent from the immediate parent tree.

Exploitability follows the parser boundary visible in the BIC: strFolder is derived from the opened document path, and a directory component such as `name'; <attacker-statement>; '` closes the quoted -Path value. PowerShell then parses the appended statement because the whole interpolated value is supplied as executable `-Command` text, rather than as an opaque working-directory argument.

Direct fix: `git show 2e8716858fc58cbb98134f94ac15729765fcac2c -- sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` copies strFolder to strFolderEscaped, replaces every PowerShell single quote `'` with `''`, and changes the command template to interpolate strFolderEscaped. That directly neutralizes the delimiter used to escape the single-quoted PowerShell literal.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7` includes the v2.4.0 prereleases, v2.4.0, v2.4.1, v2.4.2, and v2.4.3, while v2.3.2.0 does not contain the BIC (its merge-base with the BIC is 79177605093687a1d6f8b7003828b0a0a2b28ce9, not the BIC). `git tag --contains 2e8716858fc58cbb98134f94ac15729765fcac2c` returns only v2.4.3. The v2.4.2 tag resolves to a3e63915b3c3236a9f14fbb27a01cf7acb030f45 and retains the raw strFolder template; v2.4.3 resolves to fe1a4a281c6e6bec2a1a1bc39059fe7424bb5075 and contains the escaping fix.

reasoning: The advisory mechanism and patch identify the vulnerable sink precisely: a document-directory path crosses into executable PowerShell -Command source as a single-quoted literal. Line history then separates the scaffold from the flaw. de6749296b8b9a3ffa2c281d26758770a956f31a created the named function by copying command-prompt behavior, but it did not execute PowerShell or contain the Set-Location template. Its child 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 is therefore the smallest real BIC because it first selects powershell.exe and writes the unescaped single-quoted interpolation in one direct edit. Direct parent-tree diff verifies absence; later comment/type edits, the feature merge, and the later file move do not originate the vulnerable semantics. Tag containment places the BIC in the 2.4 release line including v2.4.2, and places the direct escaping fix 2e8716858fc58cbb98134f94ac15729765fcac2c only in the patched v2.4.3 boundary. Finally, the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer. Under the required BIC-only attribution rule, the lifecycle is closed as NOT_AI.
